instruction.text: Fill in the gaps to work out the mean number of books borrowed from the library.

atoms.a: First, add up all the numbers together.
Now, divide the sum of the numbers by the amount of numbers that there are.

end.text: The mean number of books borrowed from the library is 3.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps to work out the mean height of these monsters.

atoms.a: First, add up all the numbers together.
Now, divide the sum of the numbers by the amount of numbers that there are.

end.text: The mean height of the monsters is 1.6 m.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps to work out the mean price of these fruits.

atoms.a: First, add up all the numbers together.
Now, divide the sum of the numbers by the amount of numbers that there are.

end.text: The mean price of the fruit is 56p.

atoms.a: In this family, there is a range of ages. Is it helpful to calculate the mean age if you wanted to know more about the age of the family members?

end.text: Looking at the mean age, you wouldn’t think there were any children or elderly people in the family. Here, calculating the mean isn’t helpful because there is such a large range of ages.
